learningObjectives.title: China: revolution, civil war and communist rule
India, Southeast Asia and the wider region

questions.q: The Meiji Restoration (1868) led to the modernisation of:
questions.explain: The Meiji Restoration rapidly modernised and industrialised Japan.

questions.q: The Chinese revolution of 1911 overthrew the:
questions.explain: The 1911 revolution ended imperial rule and established a republic.

questions.q: Mao Zedong's Communists founded the People's Republic of China in:
questions.explain: The CCP's victory in the civil war led to the founding of the PRC in 1949.

questions.q: The Cultural Revolution (1966-76) was launched by Mao to:
options: Reassert his control and radicalise society
questions.explain: The Cultural Revolution mobilised youth and purged perceived enemies, causing upheaval.

questions.q: The Long March (1934-35) was undertaken by the:
questions.explain: The Long March was the CCP's strategic retreat that boosted Mao's leadership.

questions.q: Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941 brought which country into the Second World War?
questions.explain: Pearl Harbor (1941) brought the USA into WWII.

questions.q: India gained independence from Britain in:
questions.explain: India became independent in 1947, accompanied by partition.

questions.q: Mao's Great Leap Forward (1958-62) resulted in:
questions.explain: The Great Leap Forward's policies caused catastrophic famine.

questions.q: A founder of the Chinese Republic and the Nationalist movement was:
questions.explain: Sun Yat-sen is regarded as a founding figure of the Chinese Republic.

questions.q: The Second Sino-Japanese War (1937-45) was fought between China and:
questions.explain: Japan's invasion of China from 1937 formed part of the wider WWII in Asia.

questions.q: The leader of India's non-violent independence movement was:
questions.explain: Gandhi led the non-violent campaign for Indian independence.

questions.q: The 'domino theory' influenced US involvement in:
questions.explain: Fear that communism would spread from country to country shaped US policy in Vietnam.

questions.q: Japanese militarism in the 1930s led to:
questions.explain: Militarist Japan expanded into Manchuria and China during the 1930s.

questions.q: The leader who later introduced market-oriented economic reforms in China was:
questions.explain: Deng Xiaoping launched economic reforms and 'opening up' from the late 1970s.

questions.q: The Korean War (1950-53) resulted in the division of:
questions.explain: The Korean War entrenched the division of Korea along the 38th parallel.

questions.q: In the Chinese Civil War, the Communists (CCP) ultimately defeated the:
questions.explain: The CCP defeated Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists, who fled to Taiwan in 1949.

questions.q: The leader of Vietnamese independence and communism was:
questions.explain: Ho Chi Minh led Vietnam's struggle for independence and its communist movement.

questions.q: Japan surrendered in 1945 after the atomic bombing of:
questions.explain: The atomic bombings and Soviet entry led to Japan's surrender in August 1945.

questions.q: Assessing why the CCP won the Chinese Civil War involves weighing factors such as:
options: Peasant support, CCP organisation and GMD weaknesses
questions.explain: Multiple factors, including peasant support and Nationalist corruption, explain the CCP victory.

questions.q: Comparing the modernisation of Meiji Japan with that of China is an example of:
questions.explain: Comparing modernisation across countries is a key Paper 3 analytical skill.

specSource: IB Diploma History guide (first assessment 2020); HL regional depth options (Paper 3): History of Asia and Oceania
